To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) cyberhate experiences, as a part of online risk experiences, are associated with each other, and (2) that they are also linked with individual factors.

cyberhate is a multidimensional phenomenon that can be experienced as a victim, perpetrator, and audience, and that is connected to the other online risks, especially unwanted sexting and exposure to harmful content, and that is also associated with individual factors such as lower subjective well being and lower quality of offline relationships.

(a) there are significant associations between the different kinds of online risks, including cyberhate victimisation, cyberhate perpetration, and cyberhate exposure, and (b) cyberhate victimisations are associated with lower quality of offline relationships and lower self esteem, while cyberhate exposure and perpetration are associated with the usage of social media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions 1.
the links between various online risk experiences among young people, especially in the context of cyberhate.
the investigation of the links between different cyberhate experiences of youth and their links to other types of online risks and their links to the individual factors of youth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cyberhate is one of the online risks that can have negative effects on young people's subjective well being and it is also associated with the exposure to other online risks.
cyberhate is a multifaceted and yet not clearly conceptualised phenomenon that comprises of various online content that advocates and promotes antagonism and discrimination.
cyberhate is a phenomenon that is connected to other online risks and that it has negative effects on youth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study will provide an overview of cyberhate experiences of youth in Europe, and that it will contribute to the existing knowledge of cyberhate in the following ways.
we will explore the relationships between cyberhate and other online risks and their links with individual factors in the context of youth online experiences in four European countries.
cyberhate is a multifaceted and complex concept that needs to be investigated from a variety of angles and perspectives in the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cyberhate phenomenon is not a marginal one and it is connected to other types of online risk experiences, as well as to individual characteristics of youth.

cyberhate is an issue that needs to be considered as an individual online risk that can be experienced by young people and that is connected to other online risks and that can have an impact on youth's well being and their social relationships.
cyberhate is an important and relevant issue in youth online risk experiences.
